database_evidence: SQLite plus separate fresh PostgreSQL 18.6 databases for lifecycle, migration, restore and cleanup batches
test_isolation: Schema-mutating batches used independent databases. Reusing one database across unrelated migration/restore groups produced lock or residual-product failures; those failed attempts are not counted as passes.

coverage: The portable adapter proves reviewed user, readonly rootfs, dropped capabilities, no-new-privileges, fixed seccomp, resource limits, network none, no host ports/devices/sockets and exactly three bind mounts.
Container observation rejects substituted native identity, mount, user, network, capability, limit, log and ownership policy before removal.
limits: An actual reference container with a live probe must execute on the disposable Linux/root runner. Local policy assertions do not prove kernel enforcement.
Exact-candidate runner-daemon and native lifecycle results remain required.

coverage: A container record in exited state is never implicitly restarted by the start adapter; it requires fresh reviewed authority. Readiness refusal and timeout do not fabricate a running process.
The runner service configuration uses a bounded systemd restart policy and start limit rather than an unbounded service crash loop.
limits: Repeatedly killing a real app, measuring restart/backoff behavior and proving a sustained crash circuit have not been run for this candidate.
RUN-04 remains partial despite the no-implicit-restart safety property.

coverage: Runner unavailability is represented separately from confirmed stop. Pending managed work becomes unavailable or recovery-required rather than claiming a physical stop.
Authority leases are fenced and restore pause invalidates old live authority. Readiness waits recheck revocation.
limits: Independent stop of runner, Portal and app with continuous home/login/report/queue availability checks has not been performed in one native drill.
Production deployment and availability SLOs remain outside this evidence.

coverage: Restart cannot reconstruct executable native handles or reclaim unknown work. Ownership, generation, writer fence and controller epoch must match the durable intent.
Inventory/removal refuses foreign labels, names, images, mounts, IDs and pending work rather than deleting by name.
limits: A runner restart with a deliberately orphaned, stale and duplicate real Docker resource set has not been run for this candidate.
Linux inventory reconciliation remains part of exact-candidate runner-daemon/native acceptance.

coverage: A lost start/stop acknowledgement returns uncertain with no fabricated state and no retry of the physical effect.
Checkpoint preparation persists one exact unknown intent before native work. Replay cannot reissue it, and only an applied receipt matching the signed intent can be read.
Managed stop persists one exact intent. Update-start execution claims are single-use and preserve uncertain state across process authority loss.
limits: These are portable driver/journal transactions. The same interruption points also need exact-candidate native execution before final RUN-07 acceptance.
The result is development recovery evidence, not an exactly-once claim for arbitrary external effects.

coverage: Object limits are checked transactionally at account, plugin and global levels; release staging rolls back on a full SQLite database; data reservation has a bounded capacity boundary.
Container policy fixes bounded logging and resource limits, and data writer recovery evidence is opaque and bound to the exact owner.
limits: A real disk-full/log-volume/temp-volume drill on the supported Linux host has not measured cleanup and host-headroom behavior.
RUN-08 remains partial until native quota/disk/log failure evidence exists.

coverage: A review creates no installation. Confirmation with the same idempotency key returns the same operation and installation; a different confirmation under the same key is a 409.
Concurrent confirmation produces one installation and one operation. Durable progress remains queryable through queued and complete stages.
An unfinished operation or recovery-required operation cannot be hidden by a removed tombstone; reinstall requires a fresh identity and a fresh idempotency key.
limits: Browser double-click and page reload are covered by component behavior elsewhere; this evidence is the server idempotency boundary.

commands: Disposable managed lifecycle evidence in docs/app-platform/handoff/evidence/platform-install/acceptance.json and docs/app-platform/handoff/evidence/platform-lifecycle-runner/acceptance.json
coverage: A managed install consumes data preparation, candidate start, readiness, protected registration, boot and activation without an installer copying a pairing key or address.
The static install path remains independent of a configured runner.
limits: A neutral operator on a clean market has not performed the complete two-app install/open flow from the production SPA.
H12 remains blocked by the unapproved task persistence design and the missing Scheduled Digest reference app.

coverage: Download, signature, proof, data-stage, activation and retry-exhaustion failures are classified without exposing a failed candidate to user traffic. Unresolved native effects become recovery-required.
A failed update keeps the source generation only when the data compatibility gate admits it.
limits: Every named stage has not been injected against one continuous real runner drill with residue accounting.
LIFE-03 remains partial until that stage-by-stage native matrix exists.

commands: TEST_POSTGRES_DSN=... GOWORK=off GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.10 GOMAXPROCS=2 go test -p 1 ./internal/app -run '^(TestPlatformInstallQueueConcurrent(SQLite|Postgres)|TestPlatformFrontendUpdateConcurrentClaim(SQLite|Postgres)|TestPlatformFrontendUninstallConcurrentClaim(SQLite|Postgres)|TestPlatformDeleteDataOperatorConflict(SQLite|Postgres)|TestAppPlatformRemovalConcurrentCommit|TestPostgresAppPlatformRemovalConcurrentCommit)$' -count=1
coverage: Competing install, update, uninstall and delete-data workers/operators admit or claim exactly one operation.
Concurrent identical confirmation replays one result; concurrent conflicting confirmation is refused deterministically without changing live authority twice.
limits: This is server/API concurrency evidence on both drivers, not a two-browser manual review of every action pair.

coverage: Data schema must not move backwards, must explicitly list the current schema as readable and may not write on startup. An incompatible update is refused before admission.
A failed managed update enters recovery rather than blindly rerunning migration or starting old code against unproven data.
limits: The repository has no generic host migration runner. Mid-migration command, acknowledgement loss and explicit application migration adaptation still need an approved implementation and a real A/B/C drill.

coverage: Reinstall after a completed removal creates a new installation identity and preserves the old tombstone.
The deterministic plugin table is recreated empty after the last installation is removed; prior grants and payload do not carry into the new identity.
limits: A full reviewed uninstall then reinstall/launch path with fresh managed namespace identity has not been assembled as one acceptance scenario.
LIFE-14 remains partial.

coverage: SQLite and PostgreSQL 18.6 apply each declared step once, serialise concurrent migration and produce the same recorded products.
Fresh and accepted pre-ledger databases reach the current baseline, while the frozen baseline remains unchanged.
limits: This is repository schema evidence on disposable databases, not a production migration approval.

coverage: An unknown ledger row or missing/corrupt declared product refuses startup before claiming success. A failed step rolls back completely and can be retried.
Concurrent SQLite/PostgreSQL migration applies each step once and leaves the ledger consistent.
limits: This proves declared migration products, not an application-owned data rewrite or an in-place production cutover.

coverage: Old compatible dumps, current round trips and missing/wrong/newer schema products are handled as documented. Dry run writes nothing; truncated or foreign content rolls back.
A pre-migration PostgreSQL dump restores through the supported path.
limits: This is logical repository restore, not restoration of the coordinated runtime/data/key recovery set on a fresh host.

coverage: Restore rotates the controller epoch, fences installation generation, disables runtime bindings and removes their signing key material.
Pending operations become recovery-required, leases are cleared, and a restored runtime cannot regenerate the prior signing identity.
limits: The test does not leave a real runner holding newer native state and then prove that its first stop/restore/snapshot command is refused. That native bidirectional epoch drill remains open.

commands: TEST_POSTGRES_DSN=... GOWORK=off GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.10 GOMAXPROCS=2 go test -p 1 ./internal/app -run '^(Test(AppPlatformRestoreRetainsRevocations|PostgresAppPlatformRestoreRetainsRevocations|AppPlatformRestoreReleaseIntegrity|PostgresAppPlatformRestoreReleaseIntegrity|PlatformCredentialRestore(SQLite|Postgres)|PlatformCredentialMissingFloorRecord(SQLite|Postgres)|PlatformSignedReleaseRestore(SQLite|Postgres)|PlatformRuntimeRestore(SQLite|Postgres)))$' -count=1
coverage: Missing, wrong or newer credential values fail closed. A restored backup cannot remove a current revocation floor or resurrect a removed credential.
Release/frontend/descriptor corruption and a missing runtime/control key produce explicit refusal. Restore pauses authority and rotates the controller epoch.
A refused restore leaves its target unchanged.
limits: These are isolated fixture products. The full coordinated recovery-set/key-generation drill remains H16/native work.

coverage: Account and OU deletion sweep discovered principal tables and exact account-owned plugin rows without deleting another account/plugin.
Delete-data admission is exact-scope, concurrent conflicts admit once, and an uncertain external result requires review instead of automatic replay.
Plugin/global counters are recomputed and remain transactional after account/installation cleanup.
limits: Retention with pending schedules/events/notifications remains blocked because H09/H10 persistence is unapproved and not implemented.
DATA-08 remains partial until background-work retention/uncertainty is implemented under an approved structure.

open: JOB-01 through JOB-08 remain dependent on the unapproved H09/H10 persistence design and are not claimed from unrelated queue tests.
DATA-04 and DATA-05 still require a coordinated writer-fenced backup set and isolated fresh-host restore with all external effects paused.
RUN-03 through RUN-06, RUN-08 and LIFE-02/03/08/14 retain explicit native/manual or implementation gaps.
